source_name: Transparency International Slovensko — procurement transparency tools & analyses
why_relevant: TIS builds and documents the Slovak procurement transparency toolset (OtvorenéZmluvy.sk, the e-Portál verejného obstarávania, rankings of state firms and municipalities) and publishes methodologies plus red-flag criteria. Best single pointer to which datasets exist, which criteria matter, and where the corpus is mirrored.

source_name: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk — contract-scrutiny portal (TIS + Aliancia Fair-play)
why_relevant: Re-publishes CRZ plus ~130 smaller local-government/school registers, auto-scoring each contract against ~11 expert red-flag criteria (missing price, threshold-hugging values, higher-risk categories) and offering search, rating and RSS. Useful both as an alternative mirror of the contract corpus and as a ready-made risk-flagging layer. Also has a public GitHub organisation, suggesting the codebase/data model is inspectable.

source_name: Red Flags · Slovensko.Digital — state IT project & procurement scoring
why_relevant: Wiki-style community evaluation of state IT projects and their procurements against 50+ criteria on a 0-4 scale, linked to project records in MetaIS. For banking/payments this is the sharpest lens on public-sector IT and payments-infrastructure procurements (their preparation quality, scope and disputed elements) — information absent from the raw notices.

source_name: platforma.slovensko.digital — open-data & API request forum
why_relevant: Community forum where practitioners request, document and troubleshoot Slovak open data and APIs. Threads such as 'Dáta vestníka verejného obstarávania' and 'Centrálny register zmlúv API' contain the practical, current knowledge about endpoints, breakages, formats and workarounds that no official documentation carries. Prime snowballing surface for new procurement data sources.

source_name: TenderMonitor.sk
why_relevant: Commercial 24/7 monitoring of TED, ÚVO and the Vestník zákaziek. Named explicitly in the cell scope; valuable as an alerting layer over the same corpus and as a check on whether a notice appeared in a channel our own harvest missed.

source_name: Transpera.sk — procurement & resolution monitoring/analytics
why_relevant: Aggregates ÚVO, EKS, JOSEPHINE and ERANET data and adds supplier/buyer analytics and comparison of awarded vs contracted prices. Notably covers the e-procurement *platforms* (JOSEPHINE, ERANET, EKS), which the official ÚVO bulletin only partially reflects — a genuine coverage extension for low-value and platform-run purchases.

source_name: TenderRadar.sk
why_relevant: Aggregator that explicitly names its upstream feeds — ÚVO, EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém), CRZ, Vestník verejného obstarávania and TED — with filtering by CPV code, value and region. Its stated source list is a compact, authoritative map of every channel a complete Slovak procurement harvest must cover.

source_name: Nadácia Zastavme korupciu — procurement analyses
why_relevant: Anti-corruption foundation that publishes quantitative analyses built on ÚVO data (e.g. with AGM Partners, comparing contracts above ~EUR 50,000 across defined periods to measure the collapse in competitive tendering after the 2024 procurement-law changes). These analyses supply legal/regime context that changes how the raw notice counts must be interpreted — critical for any time-series on Slovak tenders.

source_name: data.europa.eu — Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS) and Slovak datasets
why_relevant: EU-level layer that harvests national portals (including data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk) and aggregates procurement data across member states using the eProcurement Ontology. Provides an independent mirror of Slovak procurement datasets and a comparison frame; also mirrors Slovak dataset metadata as RDF.

source_name: NBS – Subjekty finančného trhu (financial market entities database)
why_relevant: Master licence database of the National Bank of Slovakia listing every supervised entity by sector – banks, branches of foreign banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, agents. This is the canonical generator of the Slovak banking/payments actor universe that every A2 tender-search cell must query names against.

source_name: NBS – Register podľa PSD2 (JSON API)
why_relevant: Machine-readable daily-refreshed JSON of all Slovak PSD2 payment service providers (AISP/PISP/PIISP), payment institutions and e-money issuers with business name, address and IČO. Directly ingestible; the cheapest structured seed of payments-sector actor names for tender-name matching.

source_name: NBS – Registre dohľadu (index of all supervision registers)
why_relevant: Hub page enumerating every NBS register (PSD2, creditors, financial agents, AIF managers, RBUZ, CERI, DORA register of information). Used to snowball to sub-registers that each define a slice of the financial actor universe.

source_name: NBS – Register finančných agentov a finančných poradcov (regfap)
why_relevant: Register of financial intermediaries/advisers – captures the distribution-layer actors (including bank-tied agents) that fall outside the licence register but often appear as counterparties or subcontractors in financial-sector procurement.

source_name: NBS – Register veriteľov (regver, consumer-credit creditors)
why_relevant: Lists licensed non-bank consumer-credit providers ('nebankovky'), an actor group adjacent to banking/payments that buys similar core-systems and card technology.

source_name: NBS – DORA Register of Information (register informácií o zmluvných dojednaniach s ICT poskytovateľmi)
why_relevant: Under DORA, Slovak financial entities must report their ICT third-party service providers to NBS. Even if entity-level data is not published, the guidance/aggregate publications reveal which ICT vendor categories serve Slovak banks – a rare regulator-side pointer to the vendor universe behind bank IT procurement.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) – členovia
why_relevant: The single banking-sector association in Slovakia; its ~23 members cover >99% of the sector. The member list is the compact, curated buyer universe for A2 tender monitoring, and SBA positions/press releases signal sector-wide IT and payments initiatives.

source_name: Asociácia leasingových spoločností SR (ALS) – riadni členovia
why_relevant: Explicit member-listing page for ~32 leasing companies (bank-owned, captive and independent). Leasing arms are separate legal entities that run their own IT/payments procurement and often appear separately in tender and RPVS data.

source_name: Slovenská FinTech asociácia (Slovak FinTech Association)
why_relevant: Interest association of Slovak fintech/payments companies; its membership and working groups reveal the challenger/vendor side of the payments universe (including Mastercard/Vacuumlabs-linked Bratislava FinTech Hub) that rarely shows up in NBS licence registers.

source_name: FINAS – Fintech & Insurtech Association of Slovakia
why_relevant: Second, distinct Slovak fintech body (fintech + insurtech). Two competing associations means neither membership list alone is complete – both are needed to close the vendor-universe gap for payments and digital-finance suppliers.

source_name: Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS) – Ministry of Justice
why_relevant: Legally mandatory register (Act 315/2016) for anyone receiving public funds or contracting with the state, including beneficial owners and authorised persons. It is the highest-yield pointer for A2: any bank, payment provider or IT vendor that wins Slovak public contracts must be registered here, so it both enumerates suppliers and links them to ultimate owners.

source_name: Uvostat – RPVS partners listing (third-party mirror/aggregator)
why_relevant: Re-published, list-form view of RPVS entities alongside Uvostat's public-procurement analytics. Easier bulk enumeration than the official RPVS UI, and cross-links companies to their actual tender wins.

source_name: ÚVO – Zoznam hospodárskych subjektov (list of registered economic operators)
why_relevant: Public Procurement Office's register of economic operators that have proven personal-standing conditions – effectively a pre-qualified bidder universe valid for three years. Directly answers 'who bids for Slovak public contracts', the core actor question for A2.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (ORSR) + Ministry of Justice open data dumps
why_relevant: Authoritative company register giving legal names, IČO, statutory bodies and ownership for every Slovak bank subsidiary, payment institution and IT vendor. The IČO from ORSR is the join key that links licence registers, RPVS and tender award notices into one actor graph.

source_name: ORSF – open REST API aggregating Slovak state company registers
why_relevant: Free, no-key REST API claiming to consolidate ~14 Slovak state registers (RPO, ORSR, RÚZ, VAT lists) for 1.25M+ entities under CC-BY 4.0. A pragmatic bulk-resolution layer for actor names -> IČO when official APIs are awkward; must be treated as secondary to official registers.
